title: Comic Sans was designed for cartoon speech bubbles in Microsoft Bob
body: In 1994, Microsoft designer Vincent Connare saw a test version of Microsoft Bob, a program with cartoon guides who spoke in Times New Roman, and found it far too formal. Modeling his letters on comics such as Watchmen and The Dark Knight Returns, he drew a casual typeface using just a mouse. It missed Bob’s release but shipped with a Windows 95 add-on and spread everywhere. Today it is also used in schools and by some readers with dyslexia.
